_comment: Copy to acl.json (gitignored, chmod 600) and edit. The values below are examples.
A principal is a person or a bot's deployment slot — the audit log records
the name a key resolves to, not who is holding it at the API layer.
apiKey: never share one between two consumers. Generate with:
read  — GET /webclip/{id} only: poll a pending operation.
write — everything above, plus webclip.compose, webclip.save and
webclip.discard. Deliberately stops short of forcing a save
past a red ghost-audit verdict — see webclip.save.force below.
allow / deny: adjust the role for one principal. deny wins over allow.
A denied operation is left out of what GET /me reports, so a client
built from that list never learns it exists.
The operation names are the ones in acl.ts. A name that matches none of
them is warned about at boot — a typo in a deny list looks like a

claudinho._comment: OpenClaw's autonomous agent. Can compose and save, but can never self-authorize past a red ghost-audit verdict — that needs a principal with webclip.save.force.

add-scholion-webclip-skill._comment: The interactive Claude Code skill, when it calls this API instead of doing extraction/composition inline.

add-scholion-webclip-batch._comment: Backlog-import subagents (add-scholion-webclip/batch-playbook.md). Separate principal from the interactive skill on purpose: same MAX_COMPOSES_PER_DAY ceiling, but its own independent window, so a big batch run exhausting its budget never blocks interactive use.
